themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards surge
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 9.55)—signaling a potential infrastructure failure or widespread wiring issues affecting Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights.
evidence: 5 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.55)
Represents 1,233% spike—highest z-score spike in the dataset
No recent news or community board discussion yet suggests underreported hazard
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster geographically (single block, building, or district-wide); contact Con Edison for outage or service degradation reports
Interview residents about power fluctuations, appliance damage, or safety concerns; check if Con Ed is conducting maintenance or infrastructure work

themes_detail.label: Dead animal disposal crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 17 over 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.1 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 7.12)—suggesting a potential sanitation breakdown or wildlife die-off event in the district.
evidence: 17 dead animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.12, 700% increase)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago—timing suggests specific incident (weather event, water system issue, or disease) rather than gradual trend
Aligns with CB budget requests for garbage collection and recycling infrastructure
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks, Department of Sanitation, and NYC Health to confirm any disease outbreak, environmental event, or sanitation service gap
Canvass affected blocks identified in 311 complaints to document conditions and resident health concerns; map complaint locations to identify hotspot

themes_detail.label: Street sign infrastructure collapse
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints spiked to 5 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 700% jump (z-score: 9.04)—indicating potential systematic wayfinding failures or maintenance neglect in the district.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.04, 700% increase)
Spike is 3 weeks old, making it older than electrical and dead animal spikes but still statistically extreme
Affects pedestrian safety and wayfinding; aligns with broader street condition complaints (444 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Conduct visual audit of Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights street signs to verify scale of missing/damaged signage; cross-reference 311 complaint locations
Contact Department of Transportation to determine if maintenance backlog exists and when repairs were/will be scheduled

themes_detail.label: Asbestos exposure risk
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints jumped to 3 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—potentially indicating deteriorating building conditions or illegal renovation work in older Bay Ridge housing stock.
evidence: 3 asbestos complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42, 700% increase)
424 building permits filed in last 90 days (358 alterations) suggest active renovation activity—asbestos spike may reflect unsafe practices during rehabilitation
Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights has significant older housing stock vulnerable to asbestos; spike coincides with heat/hot water crisis (1,828 complaints)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 asbestos complaints with DOB permit records to identify whether complaints cluster around specific alteration jobs or buildings
Contact NYC Health and Mental Hygiene and Department of Buildings to determine investigation status; interview residents in affected buildings about exposure risks and notification

themes_detail.label: Illegal parking complaints decline sharply
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints dropped 39% this week to 238 versus a baseline of 387.9 per week (z-score: -6.79)—a statistically significant decline that may indicate either improved enforcement, systematic removal of vehicles, or a reporting/data collection issue.
evidence: 238 illegal parking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 387.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: -6.79, -39% decline)
Decline is statistically significant (z-score: -6.79) but in opposite direction of other spikes—warrants explanation
Illegal parking is largest complaint volume category (4,706 over 90 days) but sudden drop may indicate enforcement action or data anomaly
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and Department of Finance to determine whether enforcement action increased, alternate-side parking was suspended, or holidays affected ticketing
Verify whether 311 reporting lag or system changes explain the drop, or if residents perceive genuine enforcement improvement
